extracted.intended_audience: public company management, investor-relations professionals, corporate legal counsel, and communications teams preparing material disclosures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and issuing press releases that comply with SEC Regulation FD to disclose material nonpublic information—covering timing, channels, content, and follow-up filing obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intentional disclosure prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: No person acting on behalf of a company may make an intentional disclosure of material, nonpublic information to market professionals or shareholders unless public disclosure is made simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If material information is intentionally given to analysts or select investors, the company must simultaneously make the information public (e.g., via a press release through a widely circulated wire service).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unintentional disclosure timing
rubrics_metrics.description: For unintentional disclosure: provide disclosure as soon as reasonably possible (within 24 hours or start of next day's trading, whichever later).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If nonpublic material information is disclosed inadvertently (e.g., in a one-on-one conversation or leaked), issue public disclosure promptly—no later than 24 hours after the disclosure or the next trading day's open, whichever is later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release as an acceptable disclosure method
rubrics_metrics.description: Public disclosure can be made by issuing a press release through a 'widely circulated news or wire service.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of acceptable distribution channels include Dow Jones, Bloomberg, Business Wire, PR Newswire, and Reuters. Use a service recognized as widely circulated to ensure broad public access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-step process for planned material disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: For planned disclosures of material information: (1) first issue a press release distributed through regular channels, (2) provide adequate notice of a scheduled conference call, and (3) hold the conference call in an open manner permitting investors to listen in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the sequence: press release first, announce and give adequate notice of any live event, and conduct the event so that investors have an opportunity to listen (e.g., via webcast or open telephone line) to avoid selective disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of material information
rubrics_metrics.description: Material information includes (non-exhaustive) earnings information; mergers, acquisitions, tender offers, joint ventures, change in assets; new products or discoveries; new contracts; changes in control or management; change in auditors; events regarding securities (defaults, redemptions, splits, dividends); bankruptcies or receivership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat these categories as potentially market-moving; evaluate facts under the materiality standard and disclose publicly if they are material and nonpublic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Reg FD–compliant/SEC-approved distribution channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribute through SEC-approved channels (Reg FD-compliant wire services).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting an appropriate, widely circulated wire service helps satisfy the 'public disclosure' requirement of Regulation FD; document the distribution channel used for compliance records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time release to prevent selective disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Time release before any selective disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the press release is issued prior to or simultaneous with any communications to analysts, institutional investors, or other market professionals to avoid selective advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity about earnings figures and Reg G compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Be specific about earnings figures (per Reg G - non-GAAP reconciliation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When disclosing non-GAAP measures or forward-looking financial metrics, include required reconciliations and explanations to GAAP measures per Regulation G to avoid misleading statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 8-K filing obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: File 8-K within four business days of material event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to public press release distribution, complete any required SEC filings (e.g., Form 8-K) within the four-business-day filing window for material events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward-looking statements safe harbor
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid forward-looking statements without safe harbor language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include appropriate forward-looking statements disclaimers/safe-harbor language when making projections or forward-looking remarks, or avoid such statements unless covered by the safe harbor provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard sections in investor-relations press releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical IR press releases should include: Headline; Summary bullets; Lead paragraph with material news; Body with details; Quote from CEO; Forward-looking statements safe harbor; Reconciliation of non-GAAP measures (if used); About the company; Investor relations contact; Media contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this structure to ensure clarity and to include required legal and investor-relations information (e.g., CEO quote and safe-harbor language), and to make investor-relevant facts prominent and accessible.
